Contract Administrator – Full-Time

Location: Welshpool, Western Australia 6106
Employment Type: Full-Time
Salary: $90,000 – $120,000 per annum (depending on skills and experience)

MINPROVISE INTERNATIONAL PTY LTD is a leading total solutions provider delivering specialist maintenance and shutdown services, engineering, fabrication, project services, and sustaining capital works. We also provide a comprehensive range of equipment and products, supporting the mining, oil & gas, and construction industries across Australia and internationally.

We are currently seeking an experienced and motivated Contract Administrator to join our growing team on a full-time basis.
About the Role

As a Contract Administrator, you will be responsible for administering commercial contracts and providing contractual support across engineering, mining, maintenance, shutdown, and construction projects. You will work closely with project managers, engineers, procurement teams, subcontractors, and clients to ensure contracts are managed effectively, project risks are minimised, and contractual obligations are met.

Key Responsibilities
•	Prepare, review, and administer contracts, subcontracts, and service agreements in accordance with company policies and project requirements.
•	Monitor contract performance to ensure compliance with contractual terms, specifications, budgets, and project schedules.
•	Assist in preparing tender documentation, contract variations, extensions of time, and claims.
•	Coordinate the execution of contracts and maintain accurate contract records and documentation.
•	Liaise with clients, subcontractors, suppliers, and internal stakeholders regarding contractual matters.
•	Review project progress and identify contractual risks, delays, or compliance issues, and recommend appropriate solutions.
•	Monitor project costs, contract budgets, and payment schedules in collaboration with project managers and finance teams.
•	Prepare progress claims, payment certificates, contract reports, and commercial correspondence.
•	Assist in procurement activities, supplier evaluations, and subcontractor management.
•	Ensure all contract administration activities comply with company procedures, legislative requirements, and Australian Standards.
•	Maintain confidential contract records and support audits when required.
•	Follow workplace health and safety policies, company procedures, and quality management systems.

Skills and Experience
•	Bachelor's degree or relevant qualification in Construction Management, Engineering, Business, Commerce, or a related field.
•	Minimum 1-2 years of full-time experience as a Contract Administrator or in a similar commercial or project administration role.
•	Experience within the mining, engineering, construction, or industrial sectors is highly regarded.
•	Strong understanding of contract administration principles, procurement processes, and project delivery.
•	Ability to interpret contracts, technical specifications, and commercial documentation.
•	Excellent negotiation, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
•	High level of accuracy and attention to detail.
•	Strong written and verbal communication skills.
•	Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and contract management or project management software.

What We Offer
•	Full-time, permanent employment.
•	Competitive salary of $90,000 – $120,000 per annum.
•	Opportunities to work on major mining, shutdown, engineering, and industrial projects.
•	Ongoing professional development and career progression.
•	Supportive team environment with long-term career opportunities.

result.description:
Gilmac, Australia's top hay exporter, handles a quarter of the country's hay exports across three states, with major markets in Japan, Korea, and Taiwan.

 

We are seeking a qualified Electrician to support our hay processing plant operations, based out of our Midvale workshop travelling regionally to sites in Wagin, York and New Norcia to support routine weekly preventative maintenance while also contributing during planned shutdown maintenance and other plant upgrades. 

 

Responsibilities

Schedule and perform routine electrical maintenance on automated hay press, conveyors, strapping equipment, packaging machinery and associated plant systems.

Diagnose and repair electrical faults on fixed plant, motors, sensors, control panels, drives and ancillary equipment.

Assist with breakdown response, planned shutdowns and preventative maintenance across site equipment.

Support troubleshooting of PLC-controlled plant and coordinate contractor support where required.

Maintain electrical records, maintenance database updates and action registers.

Manage stock levels for electrical parts and critical spares.

Work with site and maintenance teams to improve plant uptime, safety, quality and continuous improvement outcomes.

Ensure all electrical work is completed safely and in accordance with Gilmac procedures, isolation requirements and relevant standards.

 

Skills & Experience:

Australian electrical trade qualification and relevant electrical licence/registration.

Experience in industrial, manufacturing, agricultural, processing or fixed plant environments.

Fault finding and maintenance experience across motors, sensors, conveyors, control systems, drives and automated machinery.

PLC, instrumentation, automation or packaging equipment experience would be highly regarded.

Ability to read electrical drawings and apply safe isolation and testing practices.

 

Requirements

Full-time availability and flexibility for after-hours callouts if needed.

Commitment to safety, quality, preventative maintenance and reliable plant operation.

Willingness to learn Gilmac plant systems and support practical improvements across our sites.

Ability to work independently or in a small team.

Current driver’s licence.

Pass pre-employment physical and medical tests, including alcohol and drug screening.



Remuneration: 

Salary package $130,000-$140,000 dependent on experience

To apply send resume to hr@gilmac.com.au

result.description:
About Us
Simmonds Steel is a leading structural steel supplier and fabricator servicing residential, commercial, industrial and mining projects throughout Western Australia. We provide structural steel solutions ranging from small residential applications to large-scale commercial and industrial developments, including design support, 3D modelling, fabrication and installation services.
We are seeking an experienced and motivated Construction Estimator to join our team on a full-time basis.
Position Overview
Responsible for preparing accurate cost estimates and tender submissions for structural steel fabrication and installation projects. The role involves analysing engineering and architectural documentation, calculating material and labour requirements, obtaining supplier and subcontractor pricing, and supporting project delivery through effective cost planning and estimating. Involvement in tender settlement, cost planning, supplier negotiations, and project budget forecasting
Key Duties and Responsibilities
•	Review and interpret structural, architectural and engineering drawings, specifications and tender documentation.
•	Perform detailed quantity take-offs for structural steel components, including beams, columns, lintels, bracing systems, platework and associated materials.
•	Calculate project costs, including materials, fabrication, labour, transport, craneage, installation and subcontractor services.
•	Prepare accurate cost estimates, quotations, budgets and tender submissions for residential, commercial, industrial and mining projects.
•	Liaise with engineers, architects, project managers, clients and contractors to clarify project requirements and specifications.
•	Assess project risks, site conditions and construction methodologies affecting project costs and delivery.
•	Prepare and maintain estimating databases, cost records and pricing schedules.
•	Assist management in tender reviews, contract negotiations and project handovers.
•	Monitor market pricing trends for steel products, fabrication processes and construction services.
•	Support project planning by providing cost forecasts, material schedules and estimating reports.
•	Ensure all estimates comply with relevant Australian Standards, building codes, safety requirements and company procedures.
Skills and Experience
•	Diploma, Advanced Diploma or higher qualification in Building, Construction, Engineering or a related discipline.
•	Minimum 3 years’ relevant experience as a Construction Estimator, Steel Estimator, Building Estimator or similar role.
•	Strong ability to read and interpret structural and engineering drawings.
•	Experience estimating structural steel fabrication and installation projects.
•	Sound knowledge of construction methods, steel products and fabrication processes.
•	Proficiency with estimating software, Microsoft Excel and construction management systems.
•	Ability to manage multiple tenders and meet deadlines.
What We Offer
•	Full-time permanent position.
•	Competitive salary package of $90000.00 per annum plus superannuation
•	Supportive and professional working environment.
•	Career growth within an established structural steel business.
If you have the skills and experience to contribute to our growing team, we encourage you to apply.
